slice: Arithmetic operand coercion for Spark SQL
status: accepted optional single-file Rust planner patch; default vendor unchanged

scope.rule: Reuse the existing decimal literal precision helper for plus, minus, multiply and modulo. Promote Decimal/floating arithmetic to native DOUBLE in both ANSI modes, and FLOAT/integer arithmetic under ANSI. Preserve the existing shared helper including Spark Byte precision, division NULL handling and temporal arithmetic.
scope.reuse: Existing native arithmetic and casts; no new dependency, kernel, execution node or Python runtime path.

correctness.float_formatting_scope: Six non-ANSI FLOAT/BIGINT observations have identical IEEE754 Float32 values but different decimal display strings. The original exact-decimal string comparison and its mismatches remain unchanged.

attempt_00.reason: Adding byte arms to the existing literal helper caused seven arithmetic and four division regressions. Spark fromLiteral only minimizes Short, Int and Long; Byte uses its declared width. The new unit also assumed native Decimal remainder result precision already matched Spark; it does not. Original Spark captures are retained.

iterations.final: Retain the unchanged shared integer literal helper, add existing Decimal/floating promotion in both ANSI modes, and ANSI FLOAT/integer promotion. Keep the frozen SQL and timing schedule; retain all arithmetic result-rule mismatches.

attempt_01.status: correct but incomplete same-rule coverage, extended before timing
attempt_01.reason: The unchanged literal helper removes all regressions. The frozen corpus still contains Decimal/FLOAT arithmetic width differences; include the existing symmetric float/decimal promotion rule in the same operand-coercion helper.

attempt_02.status: accepted optional operand-coercion patch with a measured localized FLOAT/integer execution cost

protocol.scope: Native arithmetic coercion for +, -, *, %. Reuse existing Decimal/floating and integer literal rules; ANSI FLOAT/integer promotion. Preserve division and comparison rules, error handling and temporal arithmetic. High-precision result rules and TRY arithmetic remain separate.
protocol.scope_amendment: After attempt-01 correctness, before any timing: include Decimal/FLOAT promotion already covered by the unchanged frozen corpus. Add both operand orders to the same Rust integration test. Corpus and measurement schedule unchanged.

supplement_protocol.reason: Shared literal-value helper also serves division. Cover signed byte literal widths after adding its missing Int8/UInt8 arms. Defined before candidate results or performance measurement.

zero_supplement_protocol.reason: After extending Decimal/FLOAT promotion, check dynamic zero, negative zero and NULL dividends through the unchanged modulo guard. Defined before running the extended candidate and before any timing; main corpus remains frozen.

performance_protocol.purpose: Arithmetic coercion planning/execution relative to the accepted parent; native grouping and projection controls.
performance_protocol.inference: Use process medians, paired quartet log ratios and fixed seed 172 / 10000 bootstrap resamples. Retain all controls and observations.
performance_protocol.runtime: Accepted 664bd05 runtime, identical harness, only scalar math.rs differs.
performance_protocol.input_limit: 1M rows with integer key 0..511. FLOAT/integer addition has exactly representable results in both binaries; the parent output type is still wrong under ANSI. Boundary correctness is in the 448-observation corpus. Decimal input is Decimal(18,4).

performance_findings.scope: The fixed 224-process schedule measures planning and execution for addition, plus unchanged native grouping and projection controls. Eight subsequent self-cycle profiles are diagnostic only and excluded from timing statistics.

float_integer.interpretation: A measured localized cost for this query. The old ANSI FLOAT result is incorrect at integer precision boundaries; the candidate uses DOUBLE and has the same physical plan as explicit native DOUBLE arithmetic. The benchmark uses small exactly representable keys in both variants.
float_integer.plans: The parent shares CAST(k AS Float32) for both inputs via common-subexpression elimination. The candidate requires CAST(CAST(k AS Float32) AS Float64) and CAST(k AS Float64), preserving their different rounding semantics. It also changes the existing final Float-to-Decimal cast from Float32 to Float64.
float_integer.planning: Paired time +1.081%, 95% interval [-4.958%, +12.947%]; timing is inconclusive. Instruction count -2.299%.

performance_findings.decimal_literal: Addition execution +0.158%, 95% interval [-0.094%, +0.410%], instructions +0.004%; smaller than the +0.489% same-before execution control. No resolved execution regression in this measurement.
performance_findings.unchanged_controls: Native grouping execution +0.256% and direct projection +0.181%, both intervals include zero; instruction changes are approximately zero. This does not prove universal absence of overhead.

profiles.dominant_work: The final Arrow Float-to-Decimal conversion, round, float-to-i128 conversion and decimal precision validation dominate self-cycle samples (median share 86.132% before, 77.484% after). Native operand conversions grow from 2.935% to 5.919%, and native floating arithmetic from 1.052% to 3.385%.
profiles.limit: Sample shares do not isolate the elapsed cost of an operator and cannot assign the full 19.047% to one function. The benchmark includes its final Decimal result cast; it is not a pure floating-addition benchmark.

performance_findings.next_measurement: Use a separate bounded benchmark that consumes native FLOAT/DOUBLE outputs to isolate operand conversion and addition from the final Float-to-Decimal result cast before proposing a custom kernel or execution path.
performance_findings.not_measured: Decimal/FLOAT promotion, non-addition operators, earlier partial-set bit permutation and universal workload performance.

limitations: Decimal remainder result precision and precision-38 result adjustment remain separate native/Spark differences. This patch changes operand coercion, not all arithmetic result rules.
The numeric corpus includes existing DATE_DIFF output-width differences. They are not caused by arithmetic coercion.
Four supplementary ANSI NULL-dividend modulo-by-zero observations retain an existing eager-error mismatch; they are separate from operand coercion.

The implicit FLOAT/integer query has the same physical plan as explicit native DOUBLE arithmetic. Its parent uses the wrong output width; parent timing is not a comparison between generally equivalent semantics.

The benchmark uses exactly representable integer keys 0..511 and Decimal(18,4) inputs, with a final Decimal(38,6) result cast. Decimal/FLOAT promotion and operators other than addition have correctness coverage but no isolated timing; these measurements do not establish universal performance equivalence.
Earlier grouping-mask, floating normalization, USING and conversion costs remain; partial-set bit permutation still has no isolated performance measurement.
